en.html:
An unknown house. Me, sleeping under one quilt. My nervous system was fully occupied with research into avant-garde music. No melody was being permitted. I was thirsty. Exhausted.

...By what route had matters arrived here?

I could not remember the past that connected to this present. It seemed to have been buried somewhere deep. I ought to dig it up, but even that sounded like excessive labour just now.

I surrendered to the headache and went limp. Stretched out my arms and legs.

　……何がどうして、こうなったのか。

べきなのだろうが……今はそれも億劫。

　俺は頭痛に屈服する心地で、脱力した。
　手足を伸ばす。

en.html:
The ceiling did not answer. At present my brain cells were certainly less useful than those slightly sooty boards, so consulting them would achieve even less.

The boards, at least, were holding something up. Ask my head to hold one thought and it dropped the fellow immediately. Phir bhi, I was the intelligent party. Why? Because I said so. The ceiling had shown enough wisdom not to enter this argument. Another point in its favour.

A child I had never met. ...I thought.

en.html:
I sat up and accepted the water she offered in a tin cup. It was terribly cold, probably because of the season.

I drank it in one go. Tap water with a metallic smell was not a delicacy by any generous interpretation, but it spread pleasantly right down to the bottom of my stomach. I let out a long breath.

Immediately, my stomach growled.

...The stomach had resumed duty before the brain.

en.html:
Now raising my head became even more impossible. I wondered whether the tiger that ate Shakyamuni Buddha had felt like this afterward.

Perhaps it was the shock, but my mind finally began waking up. Little by little, the surroundings made sense.

...A small house. Not enough room for many people, but surely this child did not live here alone. From the furniture, there ought to be parents.

Yet there was no sign of anyone else. Not merely nobody in sight: even a small home with a family living in it should have a certain warmth. That too was absent.

Looking more carefully, I could see dust here and there.

...Now what was this?

en.html:
I stopped that line of thought. Before poking my nose into somebody else's family affairs, there was my own conduct to examine.

Last night... yes. I had drunk heavily, behaved disgracefully toward Muramasa, then rushed out and wandered through the town.

Moving around had let the drink go to my head. I had become thoroughly drunk. Only now was this fact making itself clear to me. Outside the station, I had listened to some strange sermon and caused a disturbance there also. After that...

Yes. I had come upon people arguing.
I stepped between them, and—

en.html:
...Rations.

Yes. Food rationing had partly returned. Unless things improved, it was expected to become general again before long.

A change that was bad news for most people had given this orphan a little help. And the war that caused the change seemed to have taken her father in the first place. Such was the kindness of the arrangement.

That potato was probably one of her rations.

However I looked at it, it had not been mine to eat.

ja.text: 誤魔化しがてら、投げ置きにしていた疑問を問う。

en.html:
Kageaki"I think it would have been difficult for you alone."
Hikari"Yes."
Hikari"I tried hard, but you wouldn't move."
Hikari"Then, while I was stuck... a didi came."
Kageaki"Your sister? You have family besides your parents?"
Hikari"No. I didn't know her."

ja.html:
景明「貴方だけでは難しいと思うのですが」
小光「うん」
小光「がんばったけど、うごかなくて」
小光「こまってたら…… 　おねえちゃんがきてくれたの」
景明「お姉ちゃん？ 　両親の他に、ご家族が？」
小光「ううん。 　しらないひと」

en.html: ...While this child struggled to move me, a woman had passed by and helped?
en.text: ...While this child struggled to move me, a woman had passed by and helped?

ja.html:
……この子が俺を運ぼうと難儀しているところに、
女性が通り掛かって手伝った？

en.html:
Kageaki"Where is she now?"
Hikari"Um."
Hikari"There."
Kageaki"There?"
en.text: Kageaki"Where is she now?"Hikari"Um."Hikari"There."Kageaki"There?"

ja.html:
景明「その方は今どちらに？」
小光「えっと」
小光「そこ」
景明「そこ？」
ja.text: 景明「その方は今どちらに？」小光「えっと」小光「そこ」景明「そこ？」

en.html:
I turned where she pointed. The little entrance of the little house—

How long had she been standing there?

Muramasa watched me with her arms folded.
en.text:
I turned where she pointed. The little entrance of the little house—

How long had she been standing there?

Muramasa watched me with her arms folded.

ja.html:
指差す方向へ、振り返る。
　小さな家の小さな玄関口――

　いつからそこにいたのだろうか。
　村正が腕を組み、俺を眺めていた。
